hunts.label: Sunday, Nov 8
hunts.subtitle: A cold, still, clear dawn. The squirrels will sleep in until the sun finds the pines, and so may the rabbits.

rules.title: Sunday is not Saturday
items: **Hunter orange** on, hat and vest. It is required for firearm hunters Oct 17 to Jan 1.
**Stop by 9:30 am.** Plan to be unloaded and out by 9:00. Legal light is 6:06 am.
**Migratory birds are closed on Sundays.** That means dove, ducks, rails, woodcock, snipe and crow. Leave them alone today.
rules.note: Confirm seasons, shooting hours and the Sunday rules in the NCWRC Regulations Digest before you go. The clocks already changed on Nov 1, so the times here are what your clock shows.

conditions.source: Source: commercial weather service forecasts (the National Weather Service point forecast could not be read this run). Sun times from a published sun table.
items: **Walk-in, about 5:15 am:** around 40°F. Wind from the west-northwest at about 1 mph, so nearly still. Partly cloudy. Humidity 85 to 87%.
**9 am:** no hourly figure was available. The day is forecast mainly sunny, wind west to west-southwest 5 to 10 mph, high near 64°F.
**Precipitation:** dry. About 5 to 6% shown for the early hours.
**Moon:** new moon, about 3% lit. Dark sky. A thin sliver may rise near 5 am.
conditions.meaning: **What it likely means (my assumption, not proven):** a cold, clear, calm start. Squirrels often hold in the nest until the sun warms the pines, so expect the best activity from about 7:15 on. Rabbits sit in sun-warmed edges once the light hits. Calm air means they hear you long before they smell you.
conditions.hours_note: Only 4 and 5 am could be read. The 6 to 9 am hours were not available, so none are shown. No gust figures were listed. Trust your thread over this table.

wind.label: from the west-northwest, near calm at the walk-in, then west to west-southwest 5 to 10 mph later (assumption)

in_season: **Gray and fox squirrel** (open to Feb 28 and Jan 31). Today's main target.
**Raccoon and opossum** (opportunity only, open to Feb 28).
**Deer** is open, but you are not hunting it today. Sunday mornings are for small game. If one walks by, enjoy it.
Closed today: all migratory birds on Sundays. Woodcock opens Dec 10. Quail opens Nov 21. Turkey is a spring season.

in_season.tip: Bobcat is open. Bear opens next Saturday, Nov 14. You are not hunting either. Slugs stay zipped, for defense only.

plan.title: The plan: the Pine Feeding Table, then the bins
plan.why: **Why here:** squirrels feed at the same few trees every day. Along the main trail, about halfway from the yard to the Junction, look for a pine with a pile of cone scales or cone cores at its base. Sit 25 to 30 yards from that tree, west of the trail, back to a wide trunk, facing north. If you find no pile, use the holly cluster west of the trail. **Wind:** nearly still, from the west-northwest. Your scent drifts slowly east-southeast, behind you. **Timing:** squirrels move at light, not before, so this is not a deer sit. Leave the yard at 5:15 and be seated by 5:35, about 30 minutes before legal light. **After 7:45:** work slowly toward the Junction, then loop to the feed bins for rabbit. **Cleaning:** a squirrel or rabbit takes about five minutes to clean at the yard, so nothing here eats your Sunday.

steps.text: Leave the yard on the main trail with the red light low. Three steps, listen, three steps. Count your steps from the yard.
Halfway to the Junction, look at the base of the pines for cone scales, cone cores and husks. Pick the biggest pile. Note which tree it is under.
Sit 25 to 30 yards from that tree, back to a trunk wider than your shoulders, facing north. Load #4 at the sit, muzzle north, safety on. Tie the thread to the barrel.
Legal light. Listen first. Scan the upper third of the pines and the limbs near the trunk. In the cold, expect little before the sun hits.

The sun reaches the pines. Watch for a squirrel leaving a nest and for tails flicking. Shoot only the head or neck, and only with a trunk or the ground behind the target. Wait 10 minutes after a shot before moving.
Still-hunt toward the Junction. Three slow steps, then stop for a full minute. Keep the sun at your back where you can. Shoot N, NW, NE, E or W only.
Take the loop trail to the feed bins for rabbit. Approach from the north, into any breeze, and stop 15 yards short of thick cover. Shoot N or W only here, never toward the field or the neighbor.
Unload at the yard edge. Bag any game and keep it cool. Gloves on for the clean.
Out. The hard stop is 9:30, so there is no reason to be late. Log what you saw with a "note:" message.

items: **In the gun:** #4 birdshot. Modified choke. Safety on. This is your squirrel and rabbit load.
**Right pocket:** #7.5 birdshot, for rabbits inside 20 yards.
**No buckshot today.** Leave the 00 at home. No deer on a Sunday.
**.22 LR:** optional. If you bring it, use it only on a squirrel with a trunk or the ground behind it.
**Also carry:** knife, gloves, 12-inch thread, 10 feet of cord, a game bag, a dry layer.
warnings: Never shoot a deer with birdshot.
Never shoot at game with a house, the field, the road or the neighbor behind it.
Keep slugs zipped and separate from birdshot. Check by feel.
No birds today. Migratory birds are closed on Sundays.

animals.name: Squirrel
paragraphs: **Local:** gray squirrels are seen often. Fox squirrel is possible.
**Today:** a cold start keeps them in the nest until the sun warms the pines. Best window (assumption): 7:15 to 9:00.
**Shot:** head and neck. #4 to 30 yards, #7.5 to 25 yards. Only with a trunk or the ground behind it.

details.title: Technique: listen for the gnaw
steps: Stand or sit still and listen for a fine, dry scraping. That is a squirrel gnawing a nut or cone.
Pick the direction, then look at the upper third of the tree, not the base.
Watch for falling bits of shell or scale. Trace them up to the limb.
Wait for the head to come into the open before you raise the gun.
details.note: A chewed pine cone left as a bare spike with a few scales on top is a cob. Fresh cobs under a tree mean a regular feeder.

after: **Tip:** keep your back to the sun. A squirrel on a bright limb is easy to see and the light is behind you.
**Tip:** after a shot, mark where it fell against a trunk, then walk straight to it. Do not search.

animals.name: Rabbit
paragraphs: **Local:** likely at the feed bins and along thick edges of the loop.
**Today:** cold mornings send rabbits to sun-warmed edges once the light hits, usually after 7:30.
**Shot:** #4 to 30 yards, N or W only at the bins. Never toward the field or the neighbor.

details.title: Technique: read the clipped twig
steps: Look at small twigs and briar stems near the ground. A rabbit cuts them at a clean 45 degree angle.
A fresh cut is pale and moist. An old cut is gray.
Mark the thicket nearest the fresh cuts and approach it into the wind.
Stop 15 yards short and wait a full minute. If it bolts south, let it go.

after: **Safety:** wear gloves when you handle it and check the liver for white spots. Do not eat a rabbit with a spotted liver.

animals.name: Raccoon and opossum
paragraphs: Opportunity only. One heading to a den at dawn is possible near the swamp edge or the bins.
**Look for:** a five-fingered hand print in mud, and hair snagged on bin edges.
**Shot:** #4, head and neck, 20 yards, with a trunk or the ground behind. Never toward the house or field.

animals.name: Deer (not hunting today)
paragraphs: Deer are open, but Sunday is for small game. With only #4 and #7.5 in the gun, a deer is not a shot you can take. Never shoot a deer with birdshot.
If one walks by, stay still and watch it. Note where it came from and where it went, and send it in your "note:" message. That is scouting for a Saturday.

skill.title: Skill of the week: clean a squirrel or rabbit in five minutes
skill.principle: **Core principle:** small game is quick to clean, and quick to cool. Do it right away with gloves on and your Sunday stays yours.

sections.title: Squirrel (about 5 minutes)
steps: 1. Gloves on. Lay it belly down on a clean surface.
2. Cut across the back, through the skin only, just above the tail.
3. Put two fingers under the skin on each side of the cut. Pull one way to strip the skin over the head and the other to strip it over the tail.
4. Cut off the head, the feet and the tail.
5. Slit the belly and remove the insides. Check the liver, which should be dark and smooth.
6. Rinse in cold water and put it in a bag on ice or in the fridge within the hour.

sections.title: Rabbit (about 5 minutes)
steps: 1. Gloves on. Pinch the skin on the back and cut a small slit.
2. Put two fingers into the slit and pull the skin apart toward the head and toward the tail.
3. Cut off the feet and the head.
4. Slit the belly and remove the insides. Check the liver for white spots.
5. Rinse and cool it within the hour.

details.title: Tap to open: why cool it fast
paragraphs: A mild day warms meat quickly. Cool small game within the hour. Wash your hands and knife well afterward.

skill.checkpoint: **Checkpoint:** send a "note:" message with what you shot, how long the clean took, and one thing you would do differently.

land.intro: Continuing Saturday's scouting, now aimed at small game. Make notes on the walk.
steps: Count your steps from the yard to the Pine Feeding Table, and from the table to the Junction.
Run the thread test at 5:40 and 8:00. Write down which way it points each time.
Count the piles of cone scales or husks along the main trail and note the trees. The biggest pile is your best sit.
At the feed bins, look for clipped twigs, droppings and runs through the grass. Note where they lead.
Send a "note:" message with what you found. Next week's plan will use it.

safety: **Shooting arc:** north-northwest, north and north-northeast. Never beyond east or west. NEVER south. The house is SW, the field is SE, the neighbor is south.
Birdshot and .22 need a trunk or the ground behind the target. Do not shoot a squirrel against the sky toward the house.
Hunter orange on, hat and vest. The hard stop is 9:30 am. Be unloaded and out by 9:00.
Cold start, about 40°F. Wear a dry layer and keep your hands warm so your trigger finger works. Wet leaves and roots are slick, so walk slowly with the red light.
Knife and gloves for cleaning. Cut away from your hand. Wash up afterward.
Bear and fox are in the area. Bear season opens Nov 14, and you are not hunting it. Slugs are for defense only.
hunts.regs: Check the NCWRC Regulations Digest for season dates, Sunday hunting rules and bag limits for squirrel, rabbit, raccoon and opossum.
hunts.gaps: No hunting entries in your Daily Notes this week. The National Weather Service point forecast and two other forecast pages could not be read this run. Only the 4 and 5 am figures and the daily summary were found, so there is no 6 to 9 am table, no 9 am temperature and no gust figures. One source gave different Sunday lows, 38 and 43°F. Legal light is calculated from sunrise. I do not know if a cone-scale pile exists on the main trail, so the plan tells you how to find one and gives the holly cluster as a backup. The Digest was not checked directly.
